reviewer: Independent visual audit by geraldine_style_diagnosis subagent
scope: Static style alternatives for user review. This audit does not approve production animation or physical display rendering.
inspection: Each complete canonical PNG viewed at original detail and compared visually with the complete original favorite.
passMeaning: Complete, correctly arranged and sufficiently legible for static user comparison; subjective style reservations remain explicit below.

emotionRead.attentive: Unequal open eyes and a compact smile read as friendly attention.
emotionRead.considering: A tall higher eye and a smaller lower eye, plus a rising short mouth, clearly differ from the attentive pose.
emotionRead.skeptical: A flat half-lid, angled partner and down-slanting mouth communicate a dry skeptical reaction.
emotionRead.amused: Two differently shaped open eyes and the compact filled bowl mouth communicate pleased amusement.
emotionRead.concerned: Sloping integrated upper edges, lower gaze and a small downturn read as subdued worry or sadness.

styleDifferences: The five compositions and expression grammar closely follow the favorite. Eye apertures, contour mass and relative sizes change modestly.
Attentive's left eye is a little taller and heavier, considering's eye inequality is stronger, and concerned's right eye has a more open side cut.
The unequal eye silhouettes, small mouths and green near-black field are much closer to the favorite than the later symmetric available-blink anchor.
limitations: This is deliberately a close redraw. It offers only a small style change from the already selected sheet.
Concern may read as sadness or tiredness; the precise mood is a subjective interpretation, not a malformed feature.
Static viewing does not establish how these contours would move or remain consistent between animation frames.

emotionRead.attentive: The open eye beside a lowered integrated lid and shallow smile reads as relaxed, knowing attention.
emotionRead.considering: The narrow left aperture beside a taller open right eye and rising dash reads as weighing a thought.
emotionRead.skeptical: The long flat lid and lifted angular partner, paired with a descending mouth, remain clearly skeptical.
emotionRead.amused: The closed left crescent is a clean natural squint, not a missing or broken eye. Together with the open partner and small smile it reads as a wink or restrained amusement.
emotionRead.concerned: Unequal sloping lids and the small frown distinguish concern from the skeptical mouth and level lid.

styleDifferences: Attentive and considering use more integrated lids and narrower apertures than the favorite.
Amused replaces the favorite's open bowl mouth with a compact closed smile and introduces a closed squint.
Skeptical and concerned remain very close to the favorite's silhouettes, so the strongest differences are concentrated in three cells.
The original uneven eye construction and eye-led acting are retained more clearly than in the later symmetric available-blink anchor.
limitations: This is a restrained alternative rather than a uniformly new construction across all five expressions. Skeptical and concerned supply little additional style contrast.
The attentive half-lid can also read as mildly skeptical, and amused can read as a playful wink. Those readings are subjective and do not prevent static comparison.
The natural closed squint is allowed by the reference contract and is not a defect.

emotionRead.attentive: The large upright left eye beside a squat right eye and a curved smile reads as friendly curiosity.
emotionRead.considering: A similarly exaggerated tall-left and squat-right pair with a short neutral rising mouth communicates a thoughtful pause.
emotionRead.skeptical: The compressed half-lid beside a tall open eye and descending mouth remains recognizably skeptical.
emotionRead.amused: A broad low eye, tall curling partner and filled bowl mouth give a lively pleased reaction.
emotionRead.concerned: The strongly bent left lid, smaller sloping right eye and compact frown still communicate sadness or concern. The hook is part of one continuous eye contour, not a stray fragment.

styleDifferences: This sheet pushes the favorite's asymmetry much further, with conspicuously upright eyes beside wide squat eyes, greater filled contour mass and curling eye cuts.
The attentive and considering eye pairs repeat a similar tall-left and small-right relationship; their distinction relies more on the mouth than in the other two sheets.
Amused's right eye and concerned's left eye are substantially reshaped. They retain the original negative-aperture vocabulary but depart from its restrained silhouettes.
The uneven construction is closer to the favorite's expressive method than the later symmetric anchor, while its specific proportions are the least faithful of these three alternatives.
limitations: Large eye deformation makes this useful as an exploratory static contrast, but less useful as a close continuation of the selected face.
The direction title 'warm' is subjective. Increased skew and curling shapes can read as rubbery, surprised or eccentric rather than consistently warmer.
Attentive and considering have limited eye-silhouette contrast relative to their strong mouth contrast.
The curled concerned contour is visually much stronger than the favorite's concern pose. It is a style reservation, not clipping, an extra mark or an incomplete eye.

comparisonNotes: Close and Dry are not three-way equivalents of Warm: Close largely restores the liked construction, Dry adjusts three expressions noticeably, and Warm tests a much larger deformation range.
All three are complete static sheets fit for user feedback. No claim is made that the user prefers any of these new alternatives.
Every pass is tied to the listed canonical image bytes. A later image replacement requires reinspection and a matching hash update.
